orders: Bedside ocular motility examination with cover–uncover and alternate-cover testing
Sustained upgaze and repeated eyelid-opening examination for fatigable ptosis
Ice-pack test applied to the more ptotic eyelid
Examination of pupils in light and darkness, including a detailed cranial-nerve examination
Single-fiber electromyography of an orbicularis oculi or frontalis muscle
MRI of the brain and orbits with and without contrast
CT scan of the chest with contrast
results: 1. Bedside ocular motility examination with cover–uncover and alternate-cover testing
ocular motility examination: full in all directions
cover test / ocular alignment: orthophoric
2. Sustained upgaze and repeated eyelid-opening examination for fatigable ptosis
sustained upgaze fatigability test: no fatigable droop
3. Ice-pack test applied to the more ptotic eyelid
ice-pack test: POSITIVE
4. Examination of pupils in light and darkness, including a detailed cranial-nerve examination
cranial nerve examination: bilateral ophthalmoparesis with severe limitation of extraocular movements and right exotropia; ptosis improved
pupil examination (size, light reaction): equal and reactive
5. Serum acetylcholine-receptor antibodies
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: 10.32 nmol/L (normal <0.50) - strongly POSITIVE
6. Serum MuSK antibodies
anti-MuSK antibodies: negative
7. Repetitive nerve-stimulation electromyography
repetitive nerve stimulation: decremental response
8. Single-fiber electromyography of an orbicularis oculi or frontalis muscle
single-fibre EMG: normal jitter
9. MRI of the brain and orbits with and without contrast
MRI orbits: SEVERE THINNING of all extraocular muscles; exotropia of the right eye
MRI brain with contrast: no lesion, no cranial nerve enhancement
10. CT scan of the chest with contrast
CT chest (thymus): no thymic abnormality
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Seropositive ocular myasthenia gravis due to anti–acetylcholine receptor autoantibodies, with chronic extraocular-muscle atrophy

1. Chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia due to a mitochondrial cytopathy
2. Oculopharyngeal or other muscular dystrophy causing external ophthalmoplegia
3. Congenital or chronic restrictive strabismus with secondary extraocular-muscle atrophy
